places.description: A mid-rise apartment building in Ninh Kiều, Cần Thơ, on a mixed residential-commercial street with small shops, food businesses, courtyards and frequent pedestrian and motorbike traffic.
A Vietnamese public neighborhood school in Cần Thơ with standard classrooms, science and arts facilities, a schoolyard and after-school activities that vary by year.
A local bus corridor and river landing connecting Ninh Kiều with other parts of Cần Thơ, where heat, heavy rain, traffic and changing schedules affect ordinary travel.
A Cần Thơ public library setting with Vietnamese collections, newspapers, study tables, public computers and some English-language or translated material.
A neighborhood market and nearby river-oriented commercial streets with groceries, prepared food, household goods, repair services and small independent businesses.

householdShape: One caregiver, the subject, a younger sibling and one grandparent share an apartment; another close adult relative lives elsewhere in Cần Thơ and is part of regular household logistics.
familyRelations: The younger sibling is four years younger than the subject.
The nearby adult relative sometimes provides childcare or transport but does not live in the household.
materialCircumstances: Housing and food are generally stable, while discretionary spending and private-car access are limited; public services, motorbike or bus travel, repair, reuse and neighborhood commerce are routine.
mobilityPattern: Most daily movement is on foot, by motorbike or bus, with some river travel; the household makes occasional trips across Cần Thơ or to nearby Mekong Delta communities for work, family visits, appointments and larger purchases.
schoolingOrCommunityContext: Vietnamese public schooling, neighborhood markets, library access, riverside commerce and local transit create overlapping settings with peers and adults outside the household; optional activities depend on cost, schedule and transport.
culturalContext: Cần Thơ, Mekong Delta, Vietnam — A dense river-city district in Cần Thơ, a major urban center of the Mekong Delta, with canals and river movement embedded in metropolitan daily life. The household lives in Cần Thơ during 2004–2026, amid rapid urban development in the Mekong Delta, Vietnamese public institutions, dense neighborhood commerce, river-linked regional movement, digital expansion and ordinary coexistence of religious and secular practices. These facts constrain available experiences but do not imply personality, politics, morality or future profession. Concrete cultural anchors: Vietnamese is the ordinary household, school and civic language; English appears primarily through school study, media, tourism-facing commerce and the internet rather than as a co-primary neighborhood language. Tết and other national or family observances affect school calendars, household visits, food, commerce and public rhythms without prescribing the subject's beliefs. Mekong Delta waterways, seasonal heavy rain, markets and river-oriented commerce are ordinary infrastructure and economic context rather than scenic backdrop. Motorbikes, walking, buses and some river transport are normal mobility options; household access to private cars is limited. Buddhist, ancestor-veneration, Catholic, secular and other practices are visible in the wider city; the household is not assigned a religious identity by the WorldSpec. Cần Thơ's role as a regional education, health, commerce and service center creates contact with both urban institutions and relatives or visitors from surrounding delta communities.
intellectualEnvironment: Vietnamese school curricula, library collections, newspapers and television, public internet access, repair and market knowledge, family conversations, religious or philosophical material, regional university presence and ordinary disagreement are available unevenly; English-language material becomes increasingly accessible over the chronology.

worldAuthorship.abstractionMethod: G1-v2 specificity correction: the v1 generic river-delta structure was preserved as burned evidence, then re-authored as a concrete Cần Thơ, Vietnam setting using factual civic/geographic sources. No cohort genome, target personality, future profession, required formative event or downstream H outcome was used.
worldAuthorship.relocationWitness: Household and episode mechanics could be rebuilt in another Vietnamese delta city, but doing so would change the World because Cần Thơ, Ninh Kiều, Vietnamese institutional context and Mekong Delta cultural anchors are now deliberate factual inputs rather than interchangeable scenery.
